title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ（深田晴己研究室）
subtitle: Design Project III(Fukada Haruki)
educationalGoal:
Students will: (1) learn the ability to discover the problems for technological development in the electronics field, and the ability to resolve them
(2) acquire the basic and applied knowledge for the electrical and electronic engineering
(3) acquire the research and development ability of materials and devices in the field of optoelectronics
(4) learn to create clear and meaningful research reports
advice:
This course is the final subject of the project design process, and is regarded as a subject that integrates the items learned in all subjects.
Aim to acquire advanced expertise through experiments and studies.

(1) Research activities (Project activities):
Project activities conduct in a research team consisting of 2 to 3 persons per research theme. The contents of the main research activities of the year are shown in each semester as follows.
Previous semester: acquisition of phosphor materials production and processing basic technology.
Second semester: development of new materials, devices and systems under specific research themes.

(2) Training for Outcome Reporting
Provides the following training throughout the year:
- Training of oral presentations in front of many people
- Training of questions and answers sessions
- Training of creation of the research reports with theoretical discussions for experimental results
- Conduct discussion training through meetings on research content within the research group
requiredKnowledge:
Basic knowledge of basic electrical and electronic engineering (“Physical Engineering”, “Semiconductor Engineering”, “Electrical Materials” and “Optical and Electronic Device Engineering”)
Basic laboratory skills (knowledge of “Electrical and Electronic Measurement” and “Electrical and Electronic Engineering Experiments”).

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the research subject and make research plans
Be able to carry out the experiment in safe and appropriate methods
Be able to propose solutions for new development of phosphor materials and luminescent devices
Be able to theoretically calculate using the measured values
Be able to deliver oral presentations using clear and meaningful visual aids
Be able to create the project reports with theoretical discussions for experimental results
